This is not the never-near-the-pickup configuration of POL-NS-02; it is the within-400 m wrong-point configuration that POL-NS-03 governs, so POL-NS-02's automatic full-refund rule yields to POL-NS-03, which decides the outcome including the driver's compensation. ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your $4.00 no-show cancellation fee is refunded in full. The driver's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00205) never places his vehicle inside the 50 m arrival radius for this STANDARD pickup — there are 0 qualifying in-radius fixes and his closest approach across 92 fixes was 259.94 m — so the arrival that POL-NS-01(b) requires is not made out. The trip was also terminated by the driver under cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which POL-NS-01(d) treats as the driver's own admission that he could not find you; the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01, and the case is decided under POL-NS-03. The money figure: EV-FARE-00205 shows total_charged 4.00, cancellation_fee 4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00; the STANDARD zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee are both $4.00, so the greater figure for this trip is $4.00, and that whole amount is returned. The same result follows independently under POL-NS-06: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 s (longest qualifying run 0.0 s) against the 300 s STANDARD minimum, so the fee is refunded whether or not you were present and whether or not you answered messages.

To the driver: you kept within 400 m of the pin — your minimum separation across the trip was 259.94 m — so this is the wrong-point case governed by POL-NS-03 rather than the never-approached case of POL-NS-02. But POL-NS-03 still refunds the fee in full, because you were stationary outside the arrival radius and did not arrive at the pickup point, and it is you who bear the loss under POL-NS-03(i): the chat log shows the rider gave you the pickup point ('im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark', MSG-00205-001, read at 07:22:30), you answered 'ok coming' at 07:22:48, and you cancelled at 07:33:05 without moving to it — still 259.94 m short. The pin-ambiguity goodwill in POL-NS-03(ii) is not available to you: the trip record registers exactly one pickup point (registered_pickup_points is 1, not 2 or more), and in any event the rider did state a sub-location. Your account that the app pin showed the carpark side is not corroborated: no fix in your track carries a venue_id, so under POL-NS-03 the venue point is simply not established either way and the distance test governs alone. That same rule bars the rider's suggestion that you waited at 'block 128'; it is the same-or-different-block assertion POL-NS-03 forbids on general knowledge, and nothing is built on it here. Because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full, POL-NS-07 pays no compensation, and POL-NS-03(i) puts the loss on you; driver compensation is therefore nil.

Evidence weight: the chat log EV-CHAT-00205 is impaired at weight 0.8 (issue CONTENT_REDACTED). The redaction removed only the unit number; the block identifier that the fault finding turns on survives intact, so the finding survives the discount. The artifacts carrying the deciding fact — that the driver never arrived at the pickup point — are the GPS trace and the trip record, both at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) confidence cap is 1.0. The chat's impairment is schema-level only: it does not meet POL-NS-08(a)–(d) (4 messages matching trip_record.chat_message_count 4, contiguous msg_ids, no gap over 5 minutes across the arrival marker), so it is down-weighted under POL-GEN-02 and does not engage the impairment sentence of POL-NS-08.

No escalation: the anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below 4, and 2/104 = 0.019, below 0.08); rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below 3; disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; and the deciding fact is carried by full-weight evidence, not by an artifact impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d), so the POL-NS-09(a)–(e) triggers are not met. No context-only profile field (rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rate, prior flags) was used as a ground of decision.

No false-arrival referral is entered against the driver. POL-NS-05(ii) requires the arrival marker itself to be false — the trace placing the driver more than 300 m from the pin, or carrying him at 15 km/h or more, at the moment the marker is set — and the closest fix is 259.94 m with no derived fact fixing his position at 07:26:40. POL-NS-05's closing sentence expressly routes a driver stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius to POL-NS-03, which is where this case has been decided.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
